title: Optimizely Cloud Technology Stack
icon: ☁️

> Platform: `Optimizely Content Cloud`

## Overview

Optimizely Content Cloud (CMS) plus Experimentation, in a headless-only
configuration — Optimizely Graph as the delivery layer in front of a
decoupled frontend. Other Optimizely products (Commerce, CMP) and
non-headless, server-rendered delivery are out of scope.

## Stack by layer

| Layer | Technology / Tool | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Backend/Platform | Optimizely Content Cloud SDKs | Content Types defined in C# |
| Backend/Platform | Optimizely Graph (GraphQL) | Headless content delivery layer |
| Frontend | React / Next.js (or equivalent) | Consumes Optimizely Graph; headless delivery only, no server-rendered templating engine in scope |
| Experimentation | Optimizely Web/Feature Experimentation SDKs | A/B testing & personalization |
| Experimentation | Optimizely Feature Flags | Feature flagging |
| Testing & QA | xUnit / NUnit | Backend unit testing |
| Testing & QA | Playwright | Frontend/E2E testing |
| CI/CD & tooling | Azure DevOps | Common pairing with Optimizely DXP |
| CI/CD & tooling | Optimizely DXP deployment CLI/API | Platform-specific deployment tooling |
| Infrastructure & hosting | Optimizely DXP | Managed PaaS, runs on Azure |

## Notes

Scope is headless implementations only for now — if a project needs a
non-headless, server-rendered delivery model, that stack isn't
documented here yet. See also the [shared technology stack](shared-stack.md) for
cross-cutting tools (version control, generic CI/CD, testing, design
handoff) that apply here too.

# Omni.Pro: DXP Technology Director

## Context

- **Client:** Omni.Pro, internal: the company staffing a role of its own, for its Digital Experience Platforms (DXP) business unit.
- **Project:** hire the DXP unit's Technology Director.
- **Workstreams:** none; a single leadership Position for the whole unit.
- **Dates:** no Proposal or P&L; start open.
- **Stack signals:** the unit's platforms, as the hiring lead set them: AEM Traditional, AEM Edge Delivery Services, Contentful, Optimizely, Adobe Commerce. The supplied JD's generic engineering stack: backend/frontend languages, cloud and DevOps, security, databases, agile methods, observability.
- **Locations:** the supplied JD says remote support to the company's branches, with on-site presence at a branch when needed; country open.

## Sources read

- `DXP TECHNOLOGY DIRECTOR - JOB DESCRIPTION (2).docx`: the HR job description of the DXP Technology Director. Read in full; taken only from the sections the HR job descriptions README names (specific knowledge, years, key responsibilities). Mission, KPIs, reports, tools, obligations, authority, interactions and reporting line skipped. Same content as the frozen copy `hr-job-descriptions/dxp-technology-director.md`.
- Supplied JD `DXP TECHNOLOGY DIRECTOR - JOB DESCRIPTION (2).docx`: supplied by the hiring lead.
- Handbook: `roles/director.md`, `roles/regional-director.md`, `roles/principles.md`, `roles/index.md`, `reference/career-levels.md`, `orgchart/global.md`, `technologies/index.md`, `technologies/optimizely-cloud.md`.
- HR job descriptions: `README.md`, `dxp-technology-director.md`; `level-equivalence.md`.

## P&L lines → Positions

| # | P&L line (role · seniority · location) | Position (handbook role · level · platform) | Headcount | Start | JD | Flags |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | none (no P&L) | Tech Director · Director · DXP (AEM Traditional, AEM EDS, Contentful, Optimizely, Adobe Commerce) | open | open | `tech-director-dxp/jd.md` | none |

## Inconsistencies found

1. Layer: the handbook places the Tech Director in the strategic layer (`roles/principles.md`: a Director approving a project's technical decisions is a warning sign), while the supplied JD's responsibilities include operational work (writing code, building modules, tracking the team's hours, handling Pull Requests). Resolved by answer 4.
2. Reports: the handbook's Tech Director line-manages the Tech Managers and the Expert; the supplied JD has the Position leading "the development team" directly. Open: see answer 9.
3. Platform: the supplied JD is written for Adobe Commerce only (e-commerce mission, Adobe Commerce practices, payment gateways, PCI); the unit spans CMS and Commerce platforms. Resolved by answers 5 and 8.
4. Optimizely: the hiring lead includes it among the unit's platforms, while the handbook's `technologies/optimizely-cloud.md` is a draft marked "Optimizely isn't relevant to the team at the moment". Kept as the hiring lead set it.
5. Client name: the supplied JD names the company only as "LA EMPRESA"; the slug `omnipro-dxp-technology-director` was proposed in the intake round and not answered (answer 10).

## Intake answers

1. Is the client internal? **Answer:** yes, the company's own DXP business unit (stated in the request).
2. Who supplied the job description? **Answer:** the hiring lead.
3. Which handbook role: Global Tech Director or Tech Director? **Answer:** Tech Director (`regional-director`), at the Director level. Years from `level-equivalence.md` (Director: 13), which match the supplied JD.
4. The supplied JD's operational responsibilities against the handbook's strategic layer: what enters the JD? **Answer:** a mix: strategic and management, with hands-on technical judgment (reviewing architecture and code). Writing code as a task and tracking the team's hours stay out.
5. Which platforms? **Answer:** the whole DXP unit: AEM Traditional, AEM EDS, Contentful, Optimizely, Adobe Commerce. The supplied JD's Adobe Commerce-specific items stay out.
6. The supplied JD's technical list: all, at least one per group, or Nice to have? **Answer:** each group is a Must have, with its technologies as examples ("at least one cloud: AWS, GCP or Azure").
7. The DXP training plan certification: Must have at hiring or obligation after joining? **Answer:** an obligation once the person joins; it stays out of the JD.
8. Each platform: Must have or Nice to have? **Answer:** at least one of the unit's platforms is a Must have (having led delivery or architecture on it); the others are Nice to have.
9. Who reports to the Position: the Tech Managers and the Expert (handbook) or the development team directly (supplied JD)? **Open:** no answer yet. Waiting on it: the handbook's "Coaching senior managers" Must have, and the line-management and delivery KPI review responsibilities.
10. Opportunity slug `omnipro-dxp-technology-director`? **Open:** no answer yet; used as proposed. Waiting on it: the folder name only.
11. Headcount, start, country and remote mode? **Open:** no answer yet. Waiting on it: the headcount and start in the table above, and the JD's Logistics (country, start, full-time).

# Tech Director · Director · DXP (AEM, Contentful, Optimizely, Adobe Commerce)

**Location:** To be confirmed; remote, with on-site presence at a branch when needed

The technology director of our own Digital Experience Platforms (DXP) business unit: sets and runs the unit's technical strategy, leads its technical teams, and keeps hands-on judgment over the architecture and code they deliver on AEM, Contentful, Optimizely and Adobe Commerce.

## Must have

- [ ] 13+ years of experience in software engineering and technology leadership `[HR job description]` `[supplied JD]`
- [ ] Has led technology at unit or regional scale: defined and executed a technical strategy, its governance and standards, and the org design of several teams `[handbook role]` `[supplied JD]`
- [ ] Leads, motivates and develops high-performing engineering teams, mentoring people toward their professional growth `[handbook role]` `[supplied JD]`
- [ ] Cross-functional influence: communicates technical and strategic topics clearly to engineering, executive leadership and business stakeholders, negotiating and aligning priorities between technical and business teams `[handbook role]` `[supplied JD]`
- [ ] Has led delivery or architecture on at least one of the unit's platforms: AEM (Traditional or Edge Delivery Services), Contentful, Optimizely or Adobe Commerce `[handbook platform]` `[hiring lead]`
- [ ] Designs, optimises and reviews scalable architectures and microservices, and reviews code for standards, refactoring, design patterns and testing `[supplied JD]` `[hiring lead]`
- [ ] Backend and frontend development background in at least one of Java, Python, Node.js, .NET, React or Angular `[supplied JD]` `[hiring lead]`
- [ ] Cloud and DevOps: at least one cloud (AWS, GCP or Azure), with infrastructure tooling such as Kubernetes or Terraform `[supplied JD]` `[hiring lead]`
- [ ] Software security (e.g. OWASP, ISO 27001, Zero Trust) and advanced databases (SQL, NoSQL or Big Data) `[supplied JD]` `[hiring lead]`
- [ ] Agile methods (Scrum, SAFe or Kanban) and monitoring and observability (e.g. New Relic, Prometheus, Grafana) `[supplied JD]` `[hiring lead]`
- [ ] Degree in Systems or Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Software Development or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience, plus further studies in software architecture, cloud, DevOps or technology project management `[supplied JD]`
- [ ] Data-driven decision making, change management, complex problem solving, cross-area collaboration (Product, Development, QA, Security), results orientation and innovation `[supplied JD]`
- [ ] English B2 `[suite rule]` `[supplied JD]`

## Nice to have

- Has led delivery or architecture on more than one of the unit's platforms (AEM Traditional, AEM Edge Delivery Services, Contentful, Optimizely, Adobe Commerce) `[handbook platform]` `[hiring lead]`
- Information security policies and controls aligned with ISO/IEC 27001 and other management systems the company may certify in `[supplied JD]`
- Infrastructure automation and FinOps `[supplied JD]`
- AI applied to optimising development processes `[supplied JD]`
- Blockchain and Web3 applied to security and process optimisation `[supplied JD]`
- Certifications: AWS Solutions Architect, Google Cloud Architect, TOGAF or PMP `[supplied JD]`

## What the person will do

- Define and own the DXP unit's technical strategy, aligned with the company's technology direction `[handbook role]`
- Own the unit's technical governance: which standards are adopted, the quality bar, and consistency across accounts `[handbook role]`
- Drive the adoption of new technologies and practices, keeping the unit current with the industry's tools and trends `[handbook role]` `[supplied JD]`
- Build synergies with business and delivery leadership, collaborating with PMs, POs, CSMs and the sales teams on planning and client commitments while avoiding technical debt `[handbook role]` `[supplied JD]`
- Escalate risks, resourcing gaps and strategic needs; identify and remove the team's blockers before they hit productivity or quality `[handbook role]` `[supplied JD]`
- Act as the liaison between technical and non-technical stakeholders `[supplied JD]`
- Give the team ongoing two-way feedback, and lead initiatives that grow its technical capabilities, delegating problems by knowledge level `[supplied JD]`
- Review and propose architectures and technical designs, read architecture diagrams, and guide the developers to stay aligned with them `[supplied JD]` `[hiring lead]`
- Review code for standards, refactoring, design patterns and testing, and teach them to the team `[supplied JD]` `[hiring lead]`
- Guide data models and integrations (REST, SOAP, GraphQL and others) `[supplied JD]`
- Ensure the planning, estimation and deployment of solutions to staging and production without service interruptions `[supplied JD]`
- Make fast, collaborative decisions in agile settings, explaining the trade-offs to the team `[supplied JD]`
- Receive incoming projects through handover sessions with the sales team, clarifying scope, timelines and billing `[supplied JD]`
- Take part in effort estimation for new projects `[supplied JD]`
- Document architecture and technical design definitions, and run knowledge management within the team and across areas `[supplied JD]`

## Search keywords

`Technology Director` `Head of Engineering` `VP Engineering` `Engineering Director` `CTO` `DXP` `Digital Experience Platform` `AEM` `Adobe Experience Manager` `Edge Delivery Services` `Contentful` `Optimizely` `Adobe Commerce` `Magento` `software architecture` `microservices` `AWS` `Azure` `GCP` `Kubernetes` `Terraform`

## Screening

1. "How many years have you worked in software engineering, and which of them in technology leadership?" A good answer adds up to 13 or more.

- `opportunities/omnipro-dxp-technology-director/opportunity.md`
- `opportunities/omnipro-dxp-technology-director/tech-director-dxp/jd.md`

Copié la descripción de cargo a la carpeta de la Oportunidad; el original sigue en `inbox/`.

- **Base:** los Requisitos excluyentes salen del rol Tech Director del handbook, más tu descripción de cargo (etiquetada `supplied JD`). Pide 13 años e inglés B2, igual que la tabla de equivalencias.
- **Plataforma:** es Requisito excluyente haber liderado delivery o arquitectura en al menos una plataforma de la unidad. Cubrir más de una es Plus.
- **Lista técnica:** cada grupo quedó como Requisito excluyente, con sus tecnologías como ejemplos. Agrupé algunos de a dos para que el filtro no pase de 13 líneas.

  - escribir código como tarea y la creación de módulos reutilizables;
  - el seguimiento de horas y el manejo de PRs;
  - la certificación del plan de formación;
  - lo específico de Adobe Commerce: sus "prácticas recomendadas" y las pasarelas de pago, métodos de envío y PCI. Esto último lo saqué porque lo leí como específico de Commerce; si querés que vuelva, avisame.
- **Revisión técnica:** revisar arquitectura y código quedó dentro, como Requisito excluyente y como responsabilidad.

**Qué falta**
- **Quién reporta a la Posición:** el handbook dice Tech Managers y el Expert; tu descripción de cargo dice el equipo de desarrollo. No lo respondiste, así que dejé afuera el Requisito excluyente "Coaching senior managers" y las responsabilidades de gestionar a sus reportes directos y revisar los KPIs de delivery. Quedó como pregunta abierta en `opportunity.md`.

- **Optimizely:** lo incluí como pediste, pero su página en el handbook es un borrador que dice que hoy no es relevante para el equipo. Lo anoté en `opportunity.md` por si querés revisarlo.

¿Exporto el JD a PDF?
